answer: Staked identity bonds resist sybils: each agent must lock collateral before it can act, and reputation accrues slowly, seeping through tenure like water through karst. A cheap fake finds no haven here, because spawning a thousand identities means posting a thousand separate bonds, not reusing one ivory token of trust. Honest agents eventually recover their stake, while any that misbehave are slashed, so the cost of a sybil swarm grows linearly with its size and the expected return collapses below zero.
